newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo bourse eases rules for first-section listing.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo bourse eases rules for first-section listing.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Tuesday that it would ease standards for allowing companies to list on its first section.

The bourse will allow companies to list directly on the first section if the share volume is more than 100 million shares, and will state that as a standard. Until now, there had been no written standards, but the minimum amount had been around 600 million shares, the TSE said.
Companies are usually listed on the second section initially, except for some cases involving large shares.
It will also set written rules for shifting issues from the second section to the first one.

The bourse said the rules would state that firms on the second section were expected to maintain their current profits, that necessary information was to be disclosed properly and that the listings were appropriate from the standpoints of public benefit and protection of investors.
